title: City bands visiting: Tom Albert and Frankie Dusen
summary: Bands from the city, including Tom Albert (violin then trumpet) and Frankie Dusen on trombone, played at fairs; only Jim Humphrey taught the country bands.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: It's so hard to figure out how old people are, you know, so the records got lost and everything, you know. What about the dance bands?
Did you go there and hear any dancers down in the country there? Oh, well. Even when you were a child from outside the hall, what kind of?

Well, they used to have bands from the city come down and play like, you know, orchestras play like, when they have little fairs and everything, you know. I was a small kid, I'd go around these, you had to, bands playing and everything.
Who were some of the people that came down there?
Well, Tom Albert used to come down all the time and play music. Tom Albert, he was well known, come down and play music.
Did he play trumpet or violin or what?
Tom was playing, Tom, once the first time he came and he was playing the violin, the next time he came and he was playing the trumpet.
Who else was with him? Do you remember who else was?
Well, some of the fellas, let me see. I remember once Frankie Dusen came with him once. Really? The trombone. Frankie Dusen came with him once.
Did Frankie Dusen ever teach music down there?
Frankie never taught music. The only man who taught music down there when I knew it was Jim Mumphrey, the person for granddaddy. But he was the one who taught all them bands down there, Jim Mumphrey.
